news-1965fire-upi.title: Four Children Die in Fire
news-1965fire-upi.body:
A faulty gas line servicing a rented trailer is believed to have caused the fire which resulted in the death of four young children, Monday, at a trailer park located on Highway 11, north of Slidell.

Captain Wallace Laird, of the St. Tammany Parish Sheriff's office, said that the children were left to play in the trailer while their mothers sought out owner Ben Canterbury, of the Sahara Club, to pay the rent. They had been gone less than 20 minutes, Laird said, when occupants of other trailers noticed smoke, at 12:30 p.m., and rushed into the club to warn the mothers. By the time the women reached the trailer, however, it was a mass of flames and no rescue could be effected.

Dead were: Richard Kaske, 5; Robin Kaske, 3; Donald Kaske, 8 months; and Tonya Thomas, 3.

The parents were identified as Mr. and Mrs. Robert L. Thomas, and Richard G. Kaske — in service at Fort Eustis, Va. — and Mrs. Charlene Kaske Ronnie. The two couples had moved from El Paso, Texas, where James Ronnie was working for a contractor engaged in the construction of the Slidell Junior High School.

Fire apparatus from Slidell and Pearl River were able to do little more than put out the smouldering embers, which were so hot that they melted all of the hardware on the door.

Three of the children were huddled together on a couch, while the fourth, thought to be the baby, was found on the floor.

Slidell fire officials traced the leak to a pipe leading from a natural gas line into the trailer.

Sheriff George Broom charged the two mothers with negligent homicide. They were held under $2,500 bond each, pending an investigation by Asst. District Attorney Julian Rodrigue.

The St. Tammany Farmer carried the story on its front page under the banner "Four Children Cremated." The parish coroner, Dr. H. E. Gautreaux, ruled their deaths a result of the fire; the bodies were burned beyond recognition. No record of a trial, conviction, or acquittal has ever been found — the charges appear to have been quietly dropped.
news-1965fire-upi.note: Local St. Tammany account; the story also ran on the UPI national wire (New York Times, Texas & Oklahoma papers, Dec 14, 1965)

obit-charlene-2023.title: Charlene Ann Thury
obit-charlene-2023.body:
Of Bloomington. Passed away on April 21, 2023. She was a wonderful and shining example of what it meant to be a loving wife, mother, caring grandmother, and a good person. Her hobbies were simple — crossword puzzles, bingo, eating ice cream — but most of all, loving those around her. Her passing will long be remembered by all who knew her, and she lives on forever in the memories she leaves behind in others.

Preceded in death by husband, John. Survived by children, David Thury, Diane (Patrick) Koehn and Debi (AJ) Gohr; eight grandchildren and seven great-grandchildren; siblings, Arthur Davis and Mary Jane Burket.

Memorials preferred to the Animal Humane Society.
obit-charlene-2023.note: Known to family as "Nina" / "Nena"; buried Resurrection Cemetery, Mendota Heights, with her father
